task.description: Implement REQ-022 per the gate-approved design lib/letflow/design/req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md (commit 104d2bf, PASSed Step 1b in commit d41391f) on branch feature/WF02-REQ022-20260816. Follow WF-02 Step 2a's procedure exactly: verify branch, implement lib/letflow/**/*.ex per the design, write priv/repo/migrations/*.exs, mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix ecto.migrate against a real/Docker DB, mix format --check-formatted, self-review checklist, empirically demonstrate every acceptance criterion (not just describe it).
acceptance_criteria: priv/repo/migrations gains a tenant_schemas migration (public/default schema) that applies cleanly via mix ecto.migrate, with columns for at minimum tenant_id and schema_name
a provision_tenant_schema/1-equivalent function exists that issues a real CREATE SCHEMA and records the mapping in tenant_schemas, demonstrated against at least one non-default tenant schema name

a migration-replay function exists that re-applies priv/repo/migrations/ against a specific tenant schema via Ecto's prefix: option, demonstrated by confirming at least one table exists under the provisioned schema's own information_schema, not just under public

the moduledoc/description explicitly states, as an open question rather than a silent decision, whether REQ-015's users/groups/tenant_role migrations are retrofitted to use :prefix now or remain in public schema

result.summary: Implemented REQ-022 exactly per lib/letflow/design/req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md, no behavioral deviations from the design's own decisions. New files: priv/repo/migrations/20260816090045_create_tenant_schemas.exs (Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateTenantSchemas -- public/default schema, primary_key: false + explicit binary_id id, tenant_id references(:tenants, type: :binary_id) null: false (real DB-level FK, unlike users.tenant_id/groups.tenant_id's deliberate FK omission), schema_name :string null: false, migrations_applied_at nullable :naive_datetime, timestamps(inserted_at: :provisioned_at, updated_at: false), unique_index on :tenant_id and on :schema_name, required verbatim header comment per design section 2 including the section-7 open-question note), lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/registration.ex (Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Registration Ecto schema, deliberately not named TenantSchema per design section 1's ambiguity reasoning, field(:tenant_id, Ecto.UUID) matching this codebase's existing convention (Letflow.Identity.User/TenantRole) of no belongs_to association even where a DB FK exists, changeset/2 with cast/validate_required/unique_constraint x2/foreign_key_constraint), lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex (Letflow.TenantProvisioning context module: schema_name_for_tenant/1 pure UUID-derivation per design section 3.3 including its explicit no-reserved-default-tenant-UUID divergence from R-Co; provision_tenant_schema/1 per section 3.1 -- schema_name_for_tenant/1 short-circuit on invalid UUID before any transaction opens, then one Repo.transaction/1 wrapping the transaction-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($1)) parameterized query, CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS with the schema_name interpolation the design's own section 3.1 identifier-injection-safety invariant explicitly sanctions (schema_name is only ever schema_name_for_tenant/1's output, never a raw caller string), and an insert_or_fetch_registration/2 private helper reusing Letflow.Identity.insert_or_fetch/3 + re_select_on_conflict/2's exact idiom (on_conflict: :nothing/conflict_target: :tenant_id/returning: true, then Repo.get/2 on the freshly generated id to disambiguate a real insert from an ON-CONFLICT-suppressed one, since client-generated binary_id PKs make {:ok, struct} otherwise indistinguishable) with a foreign_key_violation?/2 check translating a tenant_schemas_tenant_id_fkey violation into {:error, :tenant_not_found}, which Repo.rollback/1 turns into the transaction's own {:error, :tenant_not_found}; replay_migrations/2 per section 3.2 -- Repo.get_by(Registration, tenant_id: ...) lookup (never provisions on the fly), Ecto.Migrator.run/4 with prefix: schema_name wrapped in try/rescue converting any raised exception into {:error, {:migration_failed, exception}} per the design's own confirmed-from-source note that Migrator.run/4 raises rather than returning {:error, _}, then mark_migrations_applied/1 (Repo.update_all via Ecto.Query) stamping migrations_applied_at; tenant_scoped_migrations/0 returning [] per section 3.4, with its own moduledoc stating both halves of the append-plus-guard-pattern contract REQ-023 onward must follow). Also added test/support/req022_migration_fixture.ex (Letflow.TenantProvisioning.MigrationFixture -- the throwaway, guard-pattern-following tenant-scoped migration fixture the design's own section 5 recommends for demonstrating AC3, since tenant_scoped_migrations/0 is empty at this point in the project's history; deliberately kept as a committed test/support/ fixture rather than deleted, since it's a legitimate reusable building block for TEST-DESIGNER's own AC3 regression test at Step 3, not scope creep into priv/repo/migrations/). mix compile --warnings-as-errors: exit 0, clean, in both MIX_ENV=dev and MIX_ENV=test (confirms the test/support fixture also compiles). mix format --check-formatted: exit 0. mix ecto.migrate: 'Migrated 20260816090045 in 2.2s', confirmed via psql \d tenant_schemas showing all five columns plus the tenant_schemas_tenant_id_fkey FK, tenant_schemas_tenant_id_index/tenant_schemas_schema_name_index unique indexes (AC1). Empirical demonstration via scratch/req022_demo.exs (mix run, real dev Postgres, git-ignored per project convention, not committed -- matches the req019/req021 demo-script precedent of never being tracked): AC2 -- provision_tenant_schema/1 on a real inserted tenant returned {:ok, %Registration{schema_name: "tenant_557baef6..."}}, a second call returned the identical row (idempotency confirmed by matching id), SELECT schema_name FROM information_schema.schemata WHERE schema_name = $1 returned exactly that row confirming the schema genuinely exists in Postgres (not just a function returning :ok), and a call with a syntactically-valid-but-nonexistent tenant_id returned {:error, :tenant_not_found} -- independently re-verified via psql afterward that the schema CREATE SCHEMA had issued for that failed attempt (tenant_8a0faef2...) does NOT exist in information_schema.schemata, empirically proving the section-3.1 atomicity invariant (CREATE SCHEMA DDL rolled back together with the failed insert, no orphan schema left behind). AC3 -- replay_migrations/2 called with test/support/req022_migration_fixture.ex's MigrationFixture as an explicit migration_source override returned {:ok, [1]}; SELECT EXISTS(...) FROM information_schema.tables confirmed req022_demo_marker exists under the tenant's own schema (true) and does NOT exist under public (false), and migrations_applied_at was stamped non-nil after replay; replay_migrations/2 against an unprovisioned (never-provisioned) tenant_id returned {:error, :tenant_not_provisioned} as specified. AC4 -- grep confirms 'Open question' / 'does not retrofit those three tables' language is present verbatim in substance in Letflow.TenantProvisioning's actual shipped @moduledoc (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex lines 27-50), not only in the design doc. Self-review: grep for Repo.query in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex shows exactly the two calls the design names -- one fully parameterized ($1 advisory lock), one identifier-interpolated CREATE SCHEMA whose safety rests on schema_name's constrained tenant_[0-9a-f]{32} shape (INV-7 addressed exactly as the design specifies, since CREATE SCHEMA's identifier position cannot be a bind parameter); no bare unguarded {:ok, x} = external-call pattern (the two heuristic grep hits are inner %Registration{} = registration case-clause bindings, not bare matches -- manually confirmed); every state transition (schema creation + registry insert) is persisted synchronously inside Repo.transaction/1, nothing made async; all new public functions carry a one-line-plus @doc; this is a wholly new module with no existing call sites to break. All demo-created DB state (the tenant_557baef6... schema including its req022_demo_marker table, the tenant_schemas row, the tenants row) was dropped/deleted from the shared dev Postgres afterward and independently re-verified empty (count 0 on both tables, zero tenant_* schemas remaining) so it doesn't leak into SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER/TEST-DESIGNER's later work against the same dev DB. No deviations from the gate-approved design were needed -- every signature, behavior, and invariant in sections 2/3/4/5 was implementable exactly as specified once identity.ex's idiom and the deps/ecto_sql source citations were followed.
result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) -- this change adds a new tenant-data path (CREATE SCHEMA driven by tenant_id, a new FK-bearing migration) so the hard gate applies; INV-7 (raw-SQL identifier interpolation, addressed and documented inline) is the invariant most directly relevant, INV-4/INV-8 also apply per security-invariants.md's applicability note.
